[LTHE.4.1] **A line-leading `then` continues the nearest positive pattern.**
The pattern-level productions, `pattern`, `sequence_pattern` and `then_step`,
are [LGRA.8.1]'s. The grammar does not say which pattern a line-leading `then`
follows, and this is stated here ([STYL.2.15.4]). A line made of `then_step`s continues
the nearest pattern above it that is positive: a `pattern_body` line becomes
the head of a sequence, and a `sequence_pattern` line gains the steps. The
one-line form and the line-leading form mean the same sequence, and may be
mixed. A line-leading `then` with no pattern above it is refused
([LTHE.4.8]), and so is one whose nearest pattern above is a `no` pattern
([LTHE.4.9]). A `latest` in a `then_step` is admitted by the grammar so that
[LTHE.5.4] can refuse it with its own code. A step's `where_clause` belongs to
that step ([LGRA.8.5.10]).
